noaa_ncei_isd_hourly.name: NOAA NCEI Integrated Surface Database (ISD) — Global Hourly
noaa_ncei_isd_hourly.source: National Centers for Environmental Information, NOAA
noaa_ncei_isd_hourly.license: Public domain (US federal government work, 17 USC §105)
noaa_ncei_isd_hourly.citation: Smith A, Lott N, Vose R (2011). The Integrated Surface Database: Recent Developments and Partnerships. Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society, 92, 704-708.
noaa_ncei_isd_hourly.stations: 10 primary ASOS stations at top US MSA airports (2020 Census ranking)
noaa_ncei_isd_hourly.msa_aggregation: Population-weighted national mean (Shaman et al. 2013, Reich et al. 2019 standard)
noaa_ncei_isd_hourly.population_source: US Census Bureau (2021). 2020 Census Apportionment Results.

pipeline_stages.name: ISD parse: hourly CSV -> daily Parquet
pipeline_stages.method: Filter REPORT_TYPE in {FM-15, FM-12}, parse TMP/DEW with QC in {0,1,4,5,9,A,C,I,M,P,R,U}, drop +9999 sentinels, daily groupby mean. Compute q_g via Bolton (1980): e=6.112*exp(17.67*Td/(Td+243.5)), q=0.622*e/(P-0.378*e)*1000, P=1013.25 hPa.

pipeline_stages.name: Daily -> weekly population-weighted national
pipeline_stages.method: Date -> MMWR (year, week) via epiweeks.Week.fromdate(). Per-station weekly mean. Population-weighted aggregate across 10 MSAs (weights from 2020 Census, sum=1.0). Missing-station weights redistributed proportionally (renormalize).

pipeline_stages.name: CDC ILI + env merge
pipeline_stages.method: Inner join on epiweek. MMWR Sunday alignment verified across CDC and NOAA per joined row.

pipeline_stages.name: Season split + scaler
pipeline_stages.design: Single dataset + boundary metadata (PLAN v2.0.5 §4.2). Lookback windows can cross boundaries (predictors only).

covid_excluded.note: COVID hole — neither val nor test

pipeline_stages.scaler: StandardScaler fit on TRAIN ONLY (mean, population std). No val/test leakage.

key_design_choices.noaa_data_source: ISD station-level + population-weighted aggregation chosen over nClimDiv area-weighted because ILI literature (Shaman 2013, Reich 2019, Du 2017) uses population-weighted national mean. Matches CDC FluView's weighted-by-state-population %wILI methodology.
key_design_choices.msa_count_10: Top 10 MSAs by 2020 Census covers 26.4% of US population. Following Shaman et al. (2013) which used 18 cities; Reich et al. (2019) used 10 representative urban centers.
key_design_choices.specific_humidity_formula: Bolton (1980) saturation vapor pressure at dew point. Standard pressure 1013.25 hPa (error <=2% for typical 990-1030 hPa range).
key_design_choices.humidity_naming_clarification: Literature variously calls 'absolute humidity' or 'specific humidity'. We use specific humidity q [g/kg] computed from temperature + dew point via Bolton 1980 (Shaman et al. 2013 standard). PLAN v2.0.5 wording 'absolute_humidity' was colloquial; v2.0.6 corrected to 'specific_humidity_g_per_kg'.
key_design_choices.covid_handling: Train: pre-COVID (-> W39-2018). Val: truncate at W10-2020. COVID W11-2020 ~ W39-2020 excluded. Test: W40-2020 ~ W35-2025. Reporting: 'Test full' and 'Test w/o COVID (W40-2021 ~ W35-2025, 204 rows)' as two rows.
key_design_choices.split_architecture: Single dataset + boundary metadata, not 3 physical files. Reason: lookback windows at val/test boundaries should still read from preceding (training) rows (predictor-only access — labels are NOT used).

cdc_2002_summer_reporting_gap.description: CDC FluView (via Delphi API) does not report ILI for MMWR weeks W21-W39 of 2002 (19 weeks). This is a one-off anomaly likely tied to ILINet's early-program operation; year-round reporting is consistent from 2003 onward.
cdc_2002_summer_reporting_gap.row_impact: Train period 868 rows = 16 full seasons (52-53 weeks each, 2002-03 ~ 2017-18) + 2001-02 partial (33 weeks: W40-2001 ~ W20-2002). The 2001-02 season is the only partial season.
cdc_2002_summer_reporting_gap.gap_count: Exactly 1 epiweek gap in train: 200220 -> 200240 (W20-2002 -> W40-2002, 19 missing weeks).
cdc_2002_summer_reporting_gap.downstream_implication: Loader (M1.3) must handle one cross-gap window — either skip across the gap or apply a begin-offset at 2002-W40.
cdc_2002_summer_reporting_gap.verification: src/data/validate_dataset.py T10 asserts the train gap set equals exactly [(200220, 200240)] and that val/test/covid_excluded are contiguous.

noaa_ncei_publish_lag_for_2025.description: NOAA NCEI ISD global-hourly archive lags real time by approximately 6-9 months for QC and aggregation. As of 2026-05-17, the latest 2025 hourly observation across our 10 stations is 2025-08-27. The 2024-25 ILI season therefore terminates at MMWR W35-2025 in our merged dataset, even though CDC has data through W39-2025.
noaa_ncei_publish_lag_for_2025.row_impact: Test period W40-2020 ~ W35-2025 = 257 rows = 4 full seasons (2020-21 has 53 weeks due to W53-2020) + 2024-25 partial (48 of 52 weeks). PLAN-stated W40-2020 ~ W39-2025 would yield 260 rows.
noaa_ncei_publish_lag_for_2025.rebuild_plan: Re-running download_noaa_isd.py + parse_isd + build_env_weekly + build_merged_weekly + build_splits is idempotent and will pick up newer NCEI data once published. Suggested cadence: re-check NCEI every 2-3 months until W39-2025 is available.
